metadata.note: The Staten Island Rail Road and the Staten Island Rapid Transit, 1860-1971: the Vanderbilt-era Clifton - Tottenville line (1860-1884, including George Law's 1873-1884 Staten Island Railway Co.), and the Staten Island Rapid Transit's main line (Tompkinsville 1884, St. George 1886 - Tottenville), North Shore Branch (1886/1890-1953), Port Ivory extension (1906-1948) and South Beach Branch (1888/1894/1925-1953). The line's 1971-present era under the Staten Island Rapid Transit Operating Authority (MTA Staten Island Railway) is NOT in this file: it is feature staten-island-railway in cities/new_york_subway.geojson, whose span was corrected from 1860-2026 to 1971-2026 in the same change. The main-line features here reuse that feature's geometry, cut at Clifton and Tompkinsville, so the eras overlay exactly. Research report: research/branches/staten_island_rapid_transit_railway.txt.

operator_split: 1860-1884 is ONE feature, company 'Staten Island Rail Road', own colour #3D7A6B, segments split at 1873. Maintainer decision (2026-10-20): the 1873 Staten Island Railway Co. (George Law) was a foreclosure reorganization of the same road; giving it its own company string 'Staten Island Railway' would make Rule 4 normalization merge it with the 1971-present SIRTOA operator, which also carries 'Staten Island Railway'. OPEN QUESTION: strictly a different corporation under a different owner ran the trains 1873-1884; if a separate colour is ever wanted it needs a company string that cannot collide with the SIRTOA feature (e.g. 'Staten Island Railway (Law)'). CAVEAT: under companycheck.py's coverage normalizer (which drops 'rail', 'road' and 'railway') 'Staten Island Rail Road' and 'Staten Island Railway' both reduce to 'staten island'; layercheck.py's Rule 4 colour check compares the strings as written and keeps them apart.

1884-1971 is ONE operator, company 'Staten Island Rapid Transit', own colour #9C2B4E (chosen 2026-10-20, verified unused by any other company in data/). Not the B&O colour. Maintainer decision: the B&O held stock (and, by some accounts, a 1885 lease) but the SIRT remained a separate corporation running its own trains under its own name and timetable section ('The Staten Island Rapid Transit Railway Company (Baltimore & Ohio System)', Feb 1952 Guide p. 422). OPEN CHOICE: the B&O report (research/branches/baltimore_and_ohio_railroad.txt [8]) proposed a B&O-colour split from Nov 21 1885; if that is ever adopted, 1899 (auction to B&O representatives, SIRT Railway formed as a B&O subsidiary) is the better-evidenced date. The 1884 lease date is the split from the Staten Island Rail Road feature; the 1899 reorganization is not split.

1971-07-01 SIRT -> SIRTOA (MTA): genuine operator change; the 1971-present era is feature staten-island-railway in cities/new_york_subway.geojson (company 'Staten Island Railway', #08179C). Both files draw 1971 (year granularity: SIRT to Jun 30, SIRTOA from Jul 1).
omitted: Report block [6], Richmond County Bank Ballpark game-day service (St. George - Ballpark, 0.1 mi, 2001-2009): genuine passenger service but a 150-yard stub invisible at map scale; mentioned in the staten-island-railway segment note instead of drawn.

Report block [9], 1902-1903 Plainfield/Cranford Jct NJ - St. George trial over the Arthur Kill bridge: named by a single secondary source and the operating company (SIRT vs B&O vs Baltimore and New York Railway) is unresolved, so no honest company or colour can be given. Not drawn; see not_yet_sourced.
Report block [10], Mount Loretto Spur visitor specials: drawable NONE - no year of operation is pinned by a dated source.

Freight-only, never drawn (Rule 1): the Arthur Kill bridge line Arlington - Cranford Jct NJ ('Freight service only', Feb 1952 Guide), the Travis Branch, Arlington Yard, the North Shore Branch after Mar 31 1953 and its 2007 freight reactivation, Port Ivory after 1948, the Mount Loretto spur's freight years, and main-line freight after 1971.
Ferries (Vanderbilt's Landing, St. George, Tottenville - Perth Amboy): not rail.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-10-20 (new layer): no freight-only segments drawn; every branch ends at its passenger end, the North Shore Branch is cut at Arlington, and the Arthur Kill / Travis lines are excluded (see omitted).
metadata.horsecar_audit: 2026-10-20 (new layer): none - the Staten Island Rail Road was steam from Apr 23 1860; no animal traction found.
not_yet_sourced: Every headway before 1951 and every avg_speed_kmh in this file is an estimate (report UNRESOLVED 10). The 30-min electric-era headway is the Sept 1951 main-line snapshot; the branches' 1951 'frequent intervals' carries no number.

1902-1903 New Jersey trial service (report [9]): which company's name the trains ran under, the exact end month, and whether any 1890s regular passenger schedule ran over the Arthur Kill bridge (first train Jan 1 1890, purpose unknown). Not drawn until the operator is resolved.

South Beach Branch opening sequence (report UNRESOLVED 3): Clifton - Arrochar 1886 (station list) vs Jan 1 1888 (two articles) - drawn 1888; Arrochar - South Beach 1889 / after Sept 1888 / 1890 / 1894 - drawn 1894. Both may be too late.
Erastina - Arlington: Arlington station 1889 vs 1890 - drawn 1890.
Port Ivory passenger end 1948 vs c.1950 - drawn 1948; start 1906 rests on station tables alone.

St. George terminal fire Jun 25 1946: the report says trains turned at Tompkinsville until the new terminal opened Jun 8 1951 and finds no passenger gap; whether St. George - Tompkinsville (and the branches' St. George end) actually carried passenger trains 1946-1951, e.g. via a temporary terminal, was not established. Drawn continuous per the report.
SIRR 1860 opening: Apr 23 1860 (History, dated sequence) vs Feb 1 1860 (SIR infobox) - same year.
Mount Loretto specials: start 1885 vs 1891, end 1939 vs 1950, no dated passenger year - omitted.
Exact position of Vanderbilt's Landing (the 1860-1884 northern terminal) relative to the present Clifton station.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 12.71 mi against c.13 mi documented (report block [1]: the Guide's 14.3 mi from St. George less the c.1.3-1.5 mi St. George - Clifton piece). No straight-line leg. Cut at the present Clifton station; this era's line did NOT reach Tompkinsville or St. George (Clifton - Tompkinsville opened 1884, St. George 1886), so the drawn line starts at Clifton. The original northern terminal was Vanderbilt's Landing, the Clifton ferry landing; its exact position relative to the present Clifton station is not established, so the start point is approximate to within a few hundred metres. LATER ALIGNMENT: the geometry is the present (post-1930s grade-separation, post-2017) Staten Island Railway track; any 19th-century local deviations were not checked.

segments.note: Staten Island Rail Road Co. (chartered Aug 2 1851, Vanderbilt-financed; railroad and the Vanderbilt's Landing ferry were one enterprise). Passenger operation began Apr 23 1860 Vanderbilt's Landing (Clifton) - Eltingville, to Annadale May 14 1860, formally opened through to Tottenville Jun 2 1860 (History article's dated sequence; the SIR article infobox's 'February 1, 1860' conflicts, same year). The partial 1860 opening is below the map's year resolution. Steam from opening, no horse traction. Receivership Mar 28 1872; sold in foreclosure to George Law Sep 17 1872; property transferred to the Staten Island Railway Co. Apr 1 1873 - an ownership change, trains continued (next segment). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no pre-1951 timetable was read for this line (report UNRESOLVED 10).
sources: Segment-level: start 1860 and the 1873 foreclosure transfer from report block [1], which dated them in the History of the Staten Island Railway article (research/branches/staten_island_rapid_transit_railway.txt). Headway and speed NOT SOURCED - estimates.

segments.note: Staten Island Railway Co. (George Law), chartered Mar 20 1873, which took over the foreclosed Staten Island Rail Road's property Apr 1 1873 and ran the same Clifton - Tottenville line. Kept in this feature under the 1860 company's name and colour by maintainer decision (see metadata.operator_split): the change was a foreclosure reorganization of the same road. The State sued to dissolve the company by May 1880; the Staten Island Rapid Transit Railroad gained control Apr 3 1883 and leased it for 99 years from Jun 30 1883, effective with the opening of Clifton - Tompkinsville (passenger service Aug 1 1884), when the operator changed (see the Staten Island Rapid Transit features). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no pre-1951 timetable was read for this line (report UNRESOLVED 10).
sources: Segment-level: 1873 transfer and 1884 lease-effective date from report block [2], dated in the History of the Staten Island Railway article (research/branches/staten_island_rapid_transit_railway.txt). Headway and speed NOT SOURCED - estimates.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 13.85 mi Tompkinsville - Tottenville; with the St. George - Tompkinsville feature (0.47 mi) the main line totals 14.32 mi against 14.3 mi documented (Feb 1952 Official Guide, 'St. George to Tottenville 14.3 miles'). No straight-line leg. LATER ALIGNMENT: the drawn track is the present Staten Island Railway (post-1930s grade-crossing eliminations); 1884-1930s local deviations were not checked. Split at Tompkinsville because Tompkinsville was the northern terminal Aug 1 1884 - Mar 7 1886.

segments.note: Tompkinsville - Clifton opened Jul 31 1884 with passenger service from Aug 1 1884, extending the 1860 Clifton - Tottenville line north; Tompkinsville was the terminal until St. George opened Mar 7 1886 (separate feature). Staten Island Rapid Transit Railroad (Erastus Wiman) from 1884; sold at auction Apr 20 1899 to Baltimore and Ohio representatives and reorganized as the Staten Island Rapid Transit Railway, a B&O subsidiary that kept running its own trains under its own name (one operator for the map - see metadata.operator_split). Steam. Ends at electrification: Electrified at 600 V DC third rail: 'Electric service began on the Perth Amboy sub-division on July 1, 1925' (History of the SIR 1900-1970). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no pre-1951 timetable was read for this line (report UNRESOLVED 10).
sources: Segment-level: start year and the 1925 electrification date from report block [3], dated in the History of the Staten Island Railway articles (research/branches/staten_island_rapid_transit_railway.txt). Headway and speed NOT SOURCED - estimates.

segments.note: Electric era of the Staten Island Rapid Transit Railway (B&O subsidiary; merged with the Baltimore and New York Railway Dec 31 1944). Electrified at 600 V DC third rail: 'Electric service began on the Perth Amboy sub-division on July 1, 1925' (History of the SIR 1900-1970). Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules eff. Sept 30 1951) prints St. George - Tottenville departures: weekdays 4 15, 5 49, 6 29 ... 8 29 a.m. 'and every 30 minutes to 4 59 p.m.' with extra peak trains; Sunday 'every 30 minutes 6 29 a.m. to 11 59 p.m.' - the 30-minute headway is that 1951 snapshot, not measured for other years. Tottenville station burned Sep 3 1929 (passengers used Atlantic) and the St. George terminal fire of Jun 25 1946 sent trains to Tompkinsville until the new terminal opened Jun 8 1951 - the report finds no passenger gap on the line. SIRT applied Sep 1954 to drop Tottenville service; the City subsidized it instead (1956 agreement from Jan 1 1957). SIRT operation ended Jun 30 1971; the Staten Island Rapid Transit Operating Authority took over Jul 1 1971 (feature staten-island-railway in cities/new_york_subway.geojson). Freight stayed with the B&O and is out of scope.
sources: Segment-level: 1925 electrification and the Jun 30 1971 end from report block [3] (History of the SIR articles); service and the c.30-min base headway confirmed for 1951 by the Feb 1952 Official Guide p. 422, which the report read with legible times. Headways in other years NOT SOURCED.

properties.line: Staten Island Rapid Transit: North Shore Branch
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-20) and OpenHistoricalMap (overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org), routed with opstrace.py where noted. St. George terminal and the first 0.2 mi: OSM SIRTOA ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&O (incl. the 'North Shore Branch' spur used by the 2001-09 Ballpark trains). West of there: opstrace.py over OSM's disused North Shore Branch ways (railway=disused, old_railway_operator=B&O) and OpenHistoricalMap railway ways along the same grade.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 4.71 mi St. George - Mariners Harbor (Erastina) against 4.6 mi documented. Route mileage by source: c.0.2 mi OSM SIRTOA terminal tracks; of the opstrace run, 1.3 mi OSM B&O-tagged track and 4.0 mi OpenHistoricalMap railway ways (the OHM ways overlay the OSM disused track). No straight-line leg; trace sits within 0.01 km of Livingston, Port Richmond, Elm Park, Mariners' Harbor and Arlington station positions (OSM disused-station nodes). Documented: Mariners Harbor/Erastina 4.6 mi and Arlington 5.2 mi from St. George (North Shore Branch article; Guide 'Arlington 5 miles'). LATER ALIGNMENT: drawn on the surviving 1930s grade-separated alignment (Port Richmond / Tower Hill viaduct era); the 1886 at-grade line ran in the same corridor but its local deviations are not drawn.

segments.note: North Shore Branch opened St. George - Elm Park Feb 23 1886 (several station tables give Feb 26 1886, same year) and to Erastina (later Mariners Harbor) in summer 1886. Staten Island Rapid Transit Railroad, from 1899 the B&O-owned Staten Island Rapid Transit Railway. Steam to 1925. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no pre-1951 timetable was read for this line (report UNRESOLVED 10).
sources: Segment-level: start year from report block [5] (North Shore Branch article; station list). Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

segments.note: Electric era: North Shore electrification completed Dec 25 1925 (report block [5]). Feb 1952 Official Guide: 'Rapid Transit Trains ... operate at frequent intervals between St. George and ... (New Brighton, Sailors' Snug Harbor, Livingston, West Brighton, Port Richmond, Tower Hill, Elm Park, Mariners' Harbor) and Arlington' - positive 1951 evidence, but no times are printed, so the 30-min headway is an ESTIMATE matched to the main line's 1951 base service. Discontinued at midnight Mar 31 1953 under a Public Service Commission order of Dec 19 1952 (city bus competition). Freight continued (embargoed east of Elm Park Oct 1989, last freight Apr 21 1992; western end reactivated for freight 2007) - not drawn. A royal special crossed Oct 21 1957 and the 2001-2009 Ballpark game-day trains used only the first 0.1 mi; neither is a drawable era.

Passenger end CONFLICT: 1948 (station tables) vs 'around the year 1950' (North Shore Branch article); the Feb 1952 Official Guide index appears to dagger Port Ivory as freight-only (OCR reading, report PRIMARY SOURCE), consistent with an end before 1951 but not fixing the year. properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror, 2026-10-20) and OpenHistoricalMap (overpass-api.openhistoricalmap.org), routed with opstrace.py where noted. Lifted c.1953-55 and gone from OSM: drawn on OpenHistoricalMap railway ways tagged start_date=1888-09-01, end_date=1953-03-31, joined to the main line at Clifton.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 0.64 mi Arrochar - South Beach against c.0.7 mi documented (3.9 - 3.2). No straight-line leg. Station positions from Wikipedia station-article coordinates (none survive in OSM); the line passes within 0.01 km of Arrochar and South Beach and ends at the projection of Wentworth Avenue. Mileposts from St. George (South Beach Branch article): Arrochar 3.2, South Beach 3.9, Wentworth Ave 4.1 mi; the main line's Clifton junction is 1.57 mi out on the drawn geometry. LATER ALIGNMENT: OHM draws the 1936-37 elevated alignment's corridor; whether the 1888 at-grade line deviated locally was not checked.

segments.note: Extension Arrochar - South Beach. CONFLICT, three dates: 'sometime after September 1888' / station table 1889 (South Beach Branch article), 1890 (station list), 1894 'completed to South Beach' (History article). Drawn from 1894, the latest; service may have begun as early as 1889 - do not extend earlier without a dated source. Steam to 1925. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no pre-1951 timetable was read for this line (report UNRESOLVED 10).
sources: Segment-level: 1894 start from report block [7] (History of the SIR; earlier conflicting dates recorded in the note). Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.

segments.note: Electric era: the first SIRT electric train ran on this branch (May 20 or May 30 1925, sources differ), regular electric service from Jun 5 1925. Elevated 1936-37 for grade-crossing removal. Feb 1952 Official Guide: rapid transit trains 'at frequent intervals between St. George and ... (Rosebank, Belair Road, Fort Wadsworth, Arrochar) Cedar Avenue and South Beach' - positive 1951 evidence (Wentworth Avenue not named), but no times printed, so the 30-min headway is an ESTIMATE. Discontinued at midnight Mar 31 1953 under the same PSC order as the North Shore Branch; abandoned shortly after, third rail removed by 1955, essentially no freight afterlife.
sources: Segment-level: 1925 electrification and the Mar 31 1953 end from report block [7] (South Beach Branch article, History of the SIR); 1951 service confirmed by the Feb 1952 Official Guide p. 422. Headway NOT SOURCED - estimate.
